# glmark2 on the host harness: findings for the V3D (Raspberry Pi 4)

What glmark2-es2's default benchmark set does to YakoGL's V3D back end on the
host harness (README.md), per scene. The library is built with the Linux
OSAL, whose V3D section models the Pi 4's carve-out with the settings of the
Pi 4's glmark2 image (`driver/samples/zephyr/glmark2/boards/rpi_4b.conf`: 96
MiB). The PowerVR and the GC7000 are in [FINDINGS.md](FINDINGS.md). The part
between the markers is generated by `run.sh` (`report.py`); the notes after
it are written by hand.

## Notes

Written by hand from the run above (2026-10-07; glmark2 from GitHub's archive
of `22c527cb`; carve-out 100663296 bytes as in `rpi_4b.conf`; every process
exited 0). Host evidence only: nothing is rendered and every job completes
inside `submit()`.

* **Every entry ran to its end, no draw refused, no shader failed.** All 69
  texts compiled and linked with the V3D back end of the in-process compiler,
  as glmark2 used them. No line of kind `refused draw`, `compile failure` or
  `link failure`; `refused` is 0 in every scene.
* **Out of GPU memory: none at 96 MiB.** No allocation was refused in any
  entry. The largest high-waters are refract (55,527,424 bytes) and terrain
  (54,360,064), then shadow (40,908,544); every other entry stays under
  30 MB. Of the carve-out's 100,134,912 allocatable bytes (96 MiB less the
  512 KiB page table and a scratch page; the 512 KiB of binner overflow
  blocks count as used), refract leaves about 44.6 MB. That agrees with the
  board file's figure for refract (about 56.2 MB on the board, where the
  scenes run one after another in one process). Caveat: one process per
  entry here, so a scene starts from an empty carve-out; what an earlier
  scene leaves held or fragmented is not shown (pi4-mem-replay replays the
  sequence).
* **Tiled copies: within the 8 MiB budget.** The V3D samples CPU-made tiled
  copies of textures (`YAKOGL_V3D_TILED_COPIES_BYTES`, 8,388,608). The
  largest high-water is 7,684,096 bytes in shadow and refract: one copy of a
  1600x1200 texture at 4 bytes a texel (7,680,000 bytes before tiling), the
  scenes' off-screen targets at twice the 800x600 window (shadow's depth
  texture: `scene-shadow.cpp`, `canvas_.width() * 2`). In both, `a stale
  tiled copy of 7684096 bytes given back before the job opened` follows:
  the target is drawn into every frame, so its copy goes stale and is made
  again (a 7.7 MB CPU tiling a frame on the board; the v3d-rt-sample item is
  about sampling a render target without it).
  terrain peaks at 6,152,192, the desktop scenes at 5,248,000.
* **GL errors: the same as the PowerVR and the GC7000 (FINDINGS.md).**
  terrain raises `GL error 0x502 in glGenerateMipmap` 11 times and refract 3
  times, on NPOT textures (800x600, 1600x1200) in this report-es2 build, and
  the textures then sample (0,0,0,1) for their mipmap min filter: the known
  black terrain and refraction, which the npot item fixes. No other GL error.
  This run predates npot's merge (GL_OES_texture_npot in report-es2
  builds); a run on a tree with it should show neither these errors nor
  the incomplete-texture lines, and terrain's and refract's mip chains add
  to their GPU-memory high-waters above.
* **No depth-resolve line.** The PowerVR's `did not resolve its depth (-16)`
  in shadow and refract (FINDINGS.md) does not appear on the V3D.
* **Sampler variants:** shadow and refract each build one sampler-key
  variant of a program (a re-link once), none refused.
* **`no such uniform`: not defects**, the same lines and reasons as in
  FINDINGS.md (glmark2 sets uniforms its programs do not declare).
* **EGL config:** 0x1, RGBA8888 with D24S8 and no multisampling, on all 33
  runs, as on the other GPUs.
* **Not shown:** the V3D's own lines that every entry prints (start-up, the
  job arenas' sizes and per-frame high-water, the binner pool "not read",
  since the host has no binner) are counted as bookkeeping by `report.py`
  and left out of the table.

## 48 MiB control

The same run with the Pi 4's former carve-out: `YAKOGL_V3D_CARVEOUT_BYTES=50331648`
(48 MiB; 49,803,264 allocatable bytes, against 100,134,912 at 96 MiB), every
other setting as in `rpi_4b.conf`, `GM2_WRITE=0` (written by hand from its
printed report, 2026-10-08; same glmark2 `22c527cb`, 3 frames, one process per
entry). All 33 entries ran to their end; no compile or link failure; every
entry except terrain and refract is byte-for-byte the 96 MiB run (no refusal,
same high-water). Per scene, refusals (the report's `refused` column) and
peaks (the most bytes allocated at once):

| scene | 96 MiB: refused, peak | 48 MiB: refused, peak |
|---|---|---|
| 22 terrain | 0, 54,360,064 | 17, 49,501,184 |
| 24 refract | 0, 55,527,424 | 2, 47,825,664 |
| 23 shadow | 0, 40,908,544 | 0, 40,908,544 |
| the other 30 entries | 0, at most 29,829,888 | 0, the same peaks |

At 48 MiB the peaks of terrain and refract are what fitted before the
allocator ran out, so they are not their demand (the 96 MiB peaks are).
Shadow, the next largest, still fits with about 8.9 MB to spare.

**The board failures reproduce, in both scenes.**

* **refract:** `osal(linux): out of GPU memory for 7684096 bytes` and `yakogl/v3d:
  no GPU memory for a tiled copy of 7684096 bytes (0 of 8388608 bytes of
  copies live, a job open)`, the two lines of the board (`tools/cts/RESULTS.md`
  near lines 464-488 and 830-854). Besides them: a 10,239,836 byte texture
  (11 levels, height 1200) refused with `GL error 0x505 in glGenerateMipmap`,
  `gl_fb_target: framebuffer <n> incomplete (status 0x8cd6)` 4 times, and
  `GL error 0x506` in `current_drawable_program` and `resolve_target` 2 times
  each. The 2 refused allocations are the 10.2 MB texture and the 7.7 MB tiled
  copy.
* **terrain:** `yakogl/v3d: no GPU memory for a tiled copy of 1404928 bytes`
  (1,671,168 of the 8 MiB of copies live), three more `out of GPU memory`
  lines (1,924,096, 1,404,928 and 2,784,256 bytes), and a refused 1,924,096
  byte depth/stencil buffer: the draw is not recorded (`GL_OUT_OF_MEMORY`,
  `GL error 0x505 in glDrawArrays` 3 times, in the pending clear 2 times,
  3 + 2 frames missing a draw or clear). 17 refusals in all.

The one that does not match the board's wording is the order of the sizes: the
board's refract line names 7,684,096 bytes first, here the 10.2 MB texture is
refused before it. I read both as the same exhaustion (the 96 MiB run shows
the texture is not refused when memory is there), not as a second failure.

**Caveat:** each scene starts from an empty carve-out here, one process per
entry. The board runs the scenes one after another in one process, so what an
earlier scene leaves held or fragmented makes its failures earlier or more
frequent, never later: the host's 48 MiB failures are a lower bound on the
board's. That the 96 MiB run has no refusal at all is host evidence for the
carve-out increase, not board evidence (pi4-mem-replay replays the
sequence). This run is also on the tree before npot's merge (see the notes
above): the GL errors 0x502 of the NPOT `glGenerateMipmap` calls are in the
refract run too (2 of them).
